memories.memory: I still have about $38,000 left on the mortgage for my townhouse, even though I had hoped to pay it off before retiring.
My monthly pension and Social Security cover the essentials, but I keep a separate savings account with roughly $24,000 for home repairs and emergencies.
Last year I paid nearly $3,200 in unexpected dental bills, which meant postponing a planned trip and using part of my emergency fund.
I helped my daughter with a $6,500 down payment on a used car after she changed jobs, and she is repaying me in installments of $250 a month.
I worked two extra years in municipal administration so I could increase my pension and avoid carrying credit-card debt into retirement.
A contractor overcharged me by $1,850 for roof repairs in 2023, and I had to take the matter through small-claims mediation to recover most of it.
I keep my household budget in a spreadsheet labeled 'Carter 2026 Plan,' with about $1,100 set aside each month for property taxes, insurance, utilities, and groceries.
